description: Pins protocol::encode_capture_blob_raw + protocol::decode_capture_blob byte mapping for the MYK1 pending-capture device-local queue codec (§9.18). The blob seals arbitrary-length dictated note text under a device-local wrap_key — the codec is PROVIDER-AGNOSTIC and vault-agnostic: it never runs Argon2id and binds NEITHER account_number_hash NOR items_key_id (the queue is created while the vault is locked). It binds the per-entry capture_id (also the queue filename) via aad_capture_blob (AAD role 'pending-capture-blob'); there is NO HKDF SubkeyRole (a root_key-derived KEK would be wrong — the queue must survive while root_key is unavailable). ciphertext_len is variable (plaintext_len + 32), capped at MAX_CAPTURE_PLAINTEXT_LEN (16 KiB); an oversize ciphertext_len is a CiphertextLenOverflow reject before allocation. 11 cases: 2 encrypt (ascii + multibyte-utf8) + 1 decrypt_ok + 3 decrypt_aead_fail (tag-tamper + cross-capture_id + wrong-wrap-key, all non-distinguishing per §6.4) + 5 parse_fail (one per distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject). Cases generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_capture_blob_vectors_for_paste -- --ignored` (in protocol/src/capture_blob.rs).

cases.description: Encode a short ASCII dictated capture under the device-local wrap_key. Expected blob = 49-byte header + plaintext_len + 32-byte CTX tag.
Encode a multibyte UTF-8 capture ('café — não 🎙️') to pin byte transparency across the AEAD boundary and a different variable ciphertext_len.

Round-trip the ASCII blob back to the dictated plaintext under the matching wrap_key. Proves the decoder's header parse + AEAD unwrap (capture_id read from the header, bound into the AAD) reconstruct the exact UTF-8 bytes.
Take the ASCII blob and flip the final byte (inside the 32-byte CTX commitment tag) via XOR 0xFF. The decoder MUST surface a non-distinguishing CannotDecrypt (spec §6.4).
cases.informational_tamper_description: final byte (inside CTX tag) flipped via XOR 0xFF

cases.description: Take the ASCII blob and flip one byte of the header capture_id (offset 5). Any 16-byte id is structurally valid, so this passes the header checks — but capture_id is read from the header and bound into the AAD (§9.18.3), so the AEAD verification fails. Proves an entry cannot be relabelled / swapped to another capture_id slot.
cases.informational_tamper_description: header capture_id byte at offset 5 flipped via XOR 0x01; AAD-bound

cases.description: Take the intact ASCII blob but decrypt under a DIFFERENT device wrap_key (0x01×32 instead of 0x42×32). Collapses to the same CannotDecrypt; ports MUST NOT distinguish.
cases.informational_tamper_description: intact blob decrypted under wrong wrap_key (0x01×32)

cases.description: First byte of the MYK1 magic corrupted to 'X'. Rejected at offset 0 before any decryption (magic-byte-before-decrypt discipline, §9.18.1).
protocol_version byte (offset 4) set to 0x02 instead of 0x01. A v0.1 decoder rejects an unknown protocol version before decrypting.

ciphertext_len field (offset 45..49) set to 0xFFFFFFFF (4 GiB), far over the MAX_CAPTURE_PLAINTEXT_LEN + 32 cap. Rejected BEFORE allocation so a hostile length cannot trigger a huge allocation (contrast the fixed-size vault-quickunlock, which rejects any length != 64).
Only the 4-byte MYK1 magic, no room for the 49-byte header. Rejected before any field read.
Valid header advertising ciphertext_len = plaintext + 32, but the blob is one byte shorter than header + ciphertext_len. Rejected before the AEAD stage.
